clue.text: Worried about grasping unknown ancient language

indicators.note: grasping means the first piece holds the next one inside it

parts.note: worried as in gnawed at, so ATE (ate at)
Z, an unknown in algebra
C, short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about a dead tongue they cannot decipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' looks like a feeling but is the past tense of eat in its gnawing sense: a dog ate (worried) a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Aztec, also called Nahuatl, was the tongue of the pre-Columbian empire of Mexico.

clue.text: A white cat in a street isn't rare, ultimately

indicators.note: in means the cat goes within the following words

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
a puma is a big cat

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of rare

parts.note: its last letter is E

explanation.surface: A pale cat in the road is quite common.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' belongs to the definition: 'A white' is a white wine, while the lower-case 'a' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti spumante is a sweet sparkling white wine from Piedmont.

clue.text: What could be Bangkok hotel's sound promotional material

indicators.note: sound signals the words are to be heard aloud

parts.note: a Thai inn

explanation.surface: Musing on the noise of a Bangkok hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is merchandise or publicity linked to a film or book.

clue.text: Contradictory facial expression for one providing support

definitions.meaning: first meaning, whimsical: cross (angry) and beam (smile) together contradict
second meaning: a horizontal structural beam

explanation.walkthrough: Read whimsically, an angry smile is a contradiction; literally it is a beam across a structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbeam is a transverse beam holding up a roof or frame.

clue.text: Resent shift, say, ending for worker inside

indicators.note: inside means these pieces go within the word for shift

parts.note: to budge is to shift or move
EG, for example, i.e. say

indicators.note: ending for means take the last letter of worker

parts.note: its last letter is R

explanation.surface: A worker grumbling about a change of shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' reads as a work rota in the surface but is the verb to move slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge something is to feel resentful or envious about it.

clue.text: City airline crossing from South African country

indicators.note: crossing means the airline straddles the other piece

parts.note: BA, British Airways

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means reading upwards

parts.note: Togo in West Africa

explanation.surface: An airline flying across Africa from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogotá is the capital of Colombia.

clue.text: Merchandise on the way? Bravo!

indicators.note: on means the first piece is placed on top of the next in a down answer

parts.note: goods are merchandise
how means the way something is done

explanation.surface: Cheering a delivery that is on its way.
explanation.definitionFit: Good show is a dated British exclamation of approval, like well done.

clue.text: Cancelled one for each of 18

indicators.note: for means one piece stands in place of another

parts.note: the answer to 18 across
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Cancelling something, one each time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one for each' tells you to put I in place of EA in the answer to 18 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Undid means reversed or annulled, i.e. cancelled out.

clue.text: Endless zest in good French school is something sweet

indicators.note: in means the trimmed zest goes inside

parts.note: a lycée is a French secondary school

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: zest is citrus rind

explanation.surface: A French school's lemon zest pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Glycerine is a syrupy liquid with a sweet taste, used in food and medicine.

clue.text: Work allowing you to take extended leave?

definitions.text: Work allowing you to take extended leave?

parts.words: Work allowing you to take extended leave
parts.note: a work (novel) whose title literally describes a drawn-out farewell, i.e. taking leave at length

explanation.walkthrough: 'Take leave' reads like holiday from a job, but here it means saying farewell; the Raymond Chandler novel's title is a drawn-out one.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler's 1953 Philip Marlowe novel, whose title names a prolonged farewell, i.e. leave-taking stretched out.

clue.text: Awfully odd time, in theory, to cheat

indicators.note: awfully means the letters are badly messed up

explanation.surface: An odd hour to be unfaithful, in theory.
explanation.definitionFit: To do the dirty on someone is a British idiom for betraying or double-crossing them.

clue.text: Unhealthy condition of Society? That's the case across the pond

parts.words: That's the case across the pond
parts.note: 'in US it is': across the pond (the Atlantic) means in America

explanation.surface: Is high society ailing? Apparently so in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across the pond' is British slang for America, so 'that's the case across the pond' becomes IN US IT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinusitis is inflammation of the nasal sinuses, a common ailment.

clue.text: Two playing partners love to get through

parts.note: a duet is a piece played by two partners
O, love being nil in tennis

explanation.surface: A doubles pair at love needing to win through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' is used in the sense 'because of', as in 'through no fault of his own'.
explanation.definitionFit: Due to and through both mean because of or owing to.

clue.text: Reading for one's partner no longer suitable for him or her

parts.note: Reading has a university, so it is an example of a UNI; with 's that gives UNIS
an EX is a former partner

explanation.surface: Reading material once meant for a partner is no longer appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is an English town with a university; the capital letter is hidden at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Unisex clothes or facilities are designed for either sex.

clue.text: Sort of royal club for US dramatist

parts.note: ish means sort of
ER, Elizabeth Regina
a wood is a golf club

explanation.surface: A US playwright with a quasi-regal golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Isherwood was English-born but became an American citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood wrote novels and plays, including I Am a Camera with Auden collaborations.

clue.text: Unusual shop, said to be one containing bar?

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: A quirky shop rumoured to be a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; it is a bar of soap.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap dish is the small tray that holds a bar of soap.

clue.text: Pub drama involving politician in French city

parts.note: PH, public house on maps

indicators.note: involving means the drama wraps around the next pieces

parts.note: Noh is Japanese classical drama
MP, Member of Parliament
the French word for in is en

explanation.surface: A pub play starring a politician in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Phnom Penh is the capital of Cambodia, once part of French Indochina.

clue.text: Most of new school having walls painted

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: fresh means new
a coed is a mixed school

explanation.surface: A new school mostly decorated with murals.
explanation.definitionFit: Frescoed walls bear paintings done on wet plaster.

clue.text: Palace supporter following city going to West Ham

indicators.note: following means the supporter comes after the other pieces
in an across clue, going west means reading leftwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.walkthrough: 'West Ham' looks like the football club, but 'West' reverses LA and HAM stands alone.

clue.text: One leaving lingerie promotion possibly somehow reanimated

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for one departs from the word

parts.note: an undie is an item of underwear
I, the Roman numeral for one
an ad is one kind of promotion

explanation.surface: Someone walking out of an underwear advertising campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: The undead, such as zombies and vampires, are corpses brought back to a kind of life.

clue.text: Sand blaster in my opinion cuts small round marks

indicators.note: cuts means the opinion piece slices into the others

parts.note: O is round in shape
M for marks, the old German currency
IMO, the texting abbreviation

explanation.surface: A sandblasting operator giving a view on small circular marks.
explanation.definitionFit: The simoom is a hot, dry, sand-laden desert wind of Arabia and North Africa.

clue.text: European state chancellory taking back exhibits

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
exhibits says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A government office reclaiming its displays.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrol is an Austrian federal state in the Alps.

clue.text: See something worthwhile in blackguard

parts.note: lo means see or look
a use is a worthwhile purpose

explanation.surface: Finding value in a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a contemptible person, a scoundrel.

clue.text: Canvas creator's realism somehow capturing a king

indicators.note: capturing means the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside
somehow means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: K, the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An artist's realism capturing a monarch on canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvas creator' suggests a painter; it is someone who makes sails.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailmaker makes sails, traditionally from heavy canvas.

clue.text: Birds mostly peck, with one poking inside

indicators.note: poking inside means these letters push into the shortened kiss
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a peck is a quick kiss

explanation.surface: Birds pecking with one prodding inward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peck' looks like a bird's action, but it is a light kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiwis are flightless New Zealand birds.

clue.text: I, in turn, no longer having influence, make huge effort

parts.note: a go is a turn

indicators.note: in means the word for I goes inside the rest

parts.note: out of sway: no longer holding power
I is the numeral one

explanation.surface: A deposed figure saying they had their turn and lost power.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out of one's way is to take great trouble or put in extra effort.

clue.text: Sticky matter, new poetry book being sent back for late supplement?

indicators.note: being sent back means the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: mud is sticky stuff
the Edda is the Old Norse book of poems

explanation.surface: A messy poetry volume returned to the publisher.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is material added at the end of a book, an appendix.

clue.text: Sports for kids

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wears, as in sports a hat
second meaning: teases, as in he's having you on

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests games for children; both words are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Has on means is wearing, and also, informally, is teasing or fooling someone.
